title: Front Squat
summary: Barbell squat with the bar on the front of the shoulders: quads 1, glutes and adductors 0.5. More upright than a back squat, so more knee bend and more quads.

equipment_needs.text: Needs: barbell (Olympic bar); weight plates; rack with J-hooks (power rack, squat stands or bench uprights).

muscles.why: The quads straighten the knee; the upright torso means more knee bend. Vasti 1, rectus femoris 0.4.
The glutes extend the hip, less than in a back squat because the torso stays upright.
The adductor magnus helps extend the hip at depth.
The upper back holds the elbows up so the bar stays on the shoulders.
The trunk braces hard to stay upright; below the counting floor (0.2).

setup.text: Bar in a rack at upper-chest height; safeties just below your bottom position.
Bar on the front delts, close to the throat; fingertips under the bar or arms crossed.
Elbows high, then walk it out.

form_cues.why: Elbows up keeps the bar on the shoulders.

form_cues.cue: Sit straight down with an upright torso
form_cues.why: Upright torso keeps the bar over mid-foot.

form_cues.cue: Lead with the elbows out of the hole
form_cues.why: Stops the chest dropping and the bar rolling forward.

bias_tweaks.change: Cross-arm grip or straps on the bar
bias_tweaks.effect: For lifters who can't reach a clean grip; same squat.
Deep squats grew glutes and adductors more than half squats (back-squat study).
bias_tweaks.caveat: Measured with back squats; modeled for front squats.

bias_tweaks.change: Lower in 2-3 seconds and pause briefly in the stretch
bias_tweaks.effect: Keeps tension on in the lengthened position and removes bounce, so each rep starts honestly.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Rep speeds from 0.5 to 8 s gave similar growth; this is a control tool, not a growth trick.

mistakes.text: Dropping the elbows so the bar rolls forward.
mistakes.fix: Lighten the load until the elbows stay high.
Lifting shoes or small plates under the heels help some lifters.

misconceptions.myth: Front squats are easier on the back because they're lighter.
misconceptions.reality: They're more upright, so less hip bend; the bar is still on the spine, just in front.

misconceptions.myth: Every set has to go to failure to grow.
misconceptions.reality: Stopping a few reps short gave similar growth to failure in a meta-analysis; growth tends to rise as sets get closer to failure, but the exact curve is uncertain.

lower_risk.text: Ramp up before your first working set. For primary lifts the app suggests 50% x 8, 70% x 4 and 85% x 2 when the first working load is 60 kg or more, and 50% x 8 then 75% x 3 below that.
lower_risk.note: High-load warm-ups improved strength performance in a systematic review; the percentages are coaching convention.

lower_risk.text: Add load in small steps. The app suggests a heavier load only when the jump is 5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first, up to 2 past the top of the range. Default steps for this equipment are 2.5 kg or 5 lb; your gym profile can replace them.
Aim for about 3 reps in reserve in the 6-10 rep range. Keep heavy sets a few reps short; dropping the bar forward is the standard way to bail a missed rep.
Squat in a rack with the safeties set just below your bottom position.
Pick a variation, range and setup you can train comfortably.

alternatives.why: Back squat: more glutes and more load.
Machine squat with no bar on the spine.
Grew the rectus femoris where squats did not.

notes: Front vs back squat have not been compared for growth in a study the app cites.
Ratings and display bands are the library model (main >= 0.75, helper 0.4 to < 0.75, minor 0.25 to < 0.4, not counted < 0.25).
Technique and load management only. This page makes no medical or injury claims.
